nodes.Name: _UTIME_OMIT
nodes.DocComment: This matches the value in syscall/syscall_windows.go.

nodes.Name: file
nodes.DocComment:
file is the real representation of *File.
The extra level of indirection ensures that no clients of os
can overwrite this data, which could cause the finalizer
to close the wrong file descriptor.

Fields.Name: appendMode
Fields.DocComment: whether file is opened for appending

nodes.Name: fd
nodes.DocComment: fd is the Windows implementation of Fd.

nodes.Name: newFileKind
nodes.DocComment: newFileKind describes the kind of file to newFile.

nodes.Name: newFile
nodes.DocComment:
newFile returns a new File with the given file handle and name.
Unlike NewFile, it does not check that h is syscall.InvalidHandle.
If nonBlocking is true, it tries to add the file to the runtime poller.

nodes.Name: newConsoleFile
nodes.DocComment: newConsoleFile creates new File that will be used as console.

nodes.Name: net_newWindowsFile
nodes.DocComment:
net_newWindowsFile is a hidden entry point called by net.conn.File.
This is used so that the File.pfd.close method calls [syscall.Closesocket]
instead of [syscall.CloseHandle].

go:linkname net_newWindowsFile net.newWindowsFile

nodes.Name: DevNull
nodes.DocComment:
DevNull is the name of the operating system's “null device.”
On Unix-like systems, it is "/dev/null"; on Windows, "NUL".

nodes.Name: openFileNolog
nodes.DocComment: openFileNolog is the Windows implementation of OpenFile.

nodes.Name: seek
nodes.DocComment:
seek sets the offset for the next Read or Write on file to offset, interpreted
according to whence: 0 means relative to the origin of the file, 1 means
relative to the current offset, and 2 means relative to the end.
It returns the new offset and an error, if any.

nodes.Name: Truncate
nodes.DocComment:
Truncate changes the size of the named file.
If the file is a symbolic link, it changes the size of the link's target.

nodes.Name: Remove
nodes.DocComment:
Remove removes the named file or directory.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Pipe
nodes.DocComment:
Pipe returns a connected pair of Files; reads from r return bytes written to w.
It returns the files and an error, if any. The Windows handles underlying
the returned files are marked as inheritable by child processes.

nodes.Name: Link
nodes.DocComment:
Link creates newname as a hard link to the oldname file.
If there is an error, it will be of type *LinkError.

nodes.Name: Symlink
nodes.DocComment:
Symlink creates newname as a symbolic link to oldname.
On Windows, a symlink to a non-existent oldname creates a file symlink;
if oldname is later created as a directory the symlink will not work.
If there is an error, it will be of type *LinkError.

nodes.Name: openSymlink
nodes.DocComment:
openSymlink calls CreateFile Windows API with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT
parameter, so that Windows does not follow symlink, if path is a symlink.
openSymlink returns opened file handle.

nodes.Name: normaliseLinkPath
nodes.DocComment:
normaliseLinkPath converts absolute paths returned by
DeviceIoControl(h, FSCTL_GET_REPARSE_POINT, ...)
into paths acceptable by all Windows APIs.
For example, it converts

	\??\C:\foo\bar into C:\foo\bar
	\??\UNC\foo\bar into \\foo\bar
	\??\Volume{abc}\ into \\?\Volume{abc}\
